answer: At the wharf where new agents dock into the economy, each must post an identity bond whose cost scales superlinearly: registering N identities costs about N squared. A small trusted kernel of verified roots anchors the trust graph, and every agent is a vertex that must bond to one distinct scarce root. So 1,000 sybils demand 1,000 separate roots and about 1,000,000 cost units, not 1,000. An attacker splits across wallets to dodge this, but each split still needs its own scarce root, so the quadratic wall holds and the spend dwarfs any grading reward.
